evidence: app/src/pages/ability.ts:1-17 — whole feature is one self-contained page module
app/src/main.ts:22 — single route entry plus one import to delete
app/src/pages/pokemon.ts:93-108 — Abilities section is isolated; only inbound links to /abilities/
app/server.mjs:36 — server-side mirror of the route must be edited separately
app/index.html:14-16 — nav is static and doesn't link abilities, so no template edit
removability.rationale: A single grep for 'abilit' finds every touch point and each edit is a one-liner, but the removal spans five files (router, page, pokemon page, api types, server mirror) and leaves one dead CSS rule (.card-note), so it's a handful of scattered edits rather than delete-and-done.

evidence: app/src/components.ts:43-56 — every Pokémon card renders through one pokemonCard function
app/src/api.ts:143 — sprite URL construction is a single spriteUrl helper
app/src/components.ts:66-80 — species-vs-Pokémon reference mapping centralized in speciesCards
app/src/pages/home.ts:69 — re-implements idFromUrl inline instead of importing app/src/format.ts:17
app/src/main.ts:17-24 vs app/server.mjs:46-52 — route regexes duplicated across client and server
changeability.rationale: The likely bug hot-spots (cards, sprites, name mapping) each land in one obvious place, but a few small duplications (inline ID parsing, mirrored route patterns) mean those specific fixes would have to be made twice.

evidence: app/src/pages/move.ts:1-3 — pages depend only on api/components/format interfaces, never on each other
app/src/api.ts:87-103 — cache is module-local inside get(); no page touches fetch mechanics
app/src/components.ts:7-13 — Page interface (title/content/mounted) is the only router-to-page contract
app/src/main.ts:17-24 — router knows only regexes and page factories
app/server.mjs:46-52 — server/client split is clean except for the duplicated route table
coupling.rationale: Clean layering with narrow seams: pages consume typed data helpers and UI primitives, shared state (url-state 'shown', api cache, navigation counter) is small and explicit. The only real tangle is the route table living twice, once per runtime.

evidence: app/src/components.ts:66-80 — speciesCards models the app's real variation (dedup, form filtering, rename, extra note) via an optional callback, not flags
app/src/table.ts:5-40 — sortableTable is generic over columns with sort-key/null-last contract
app/src/format.ts:15-20 — humanize/englishName/orMissing centralize display rules
app/src/components.ts:29-33 — typeBadge's boolean `link` param is mild flag creep
app/src/pages/move.ts:17-35 vs app/src/pages/ability.ts:6-17 — page scaffold (h1 + panel + sections) repeats ~8 lines per resource, cheap to copy but not shared
abstraction_design.rationale: Abstractions are designed around actual variation and stretch well; the residue is a boolean flag on typeBadge and a small amount of per-page scaffold repetition rather than a resource-page abstraction.

findings.issue: Route regexes are duplicated between the client router (app/src/main.ts:17-24) and the server's 404 prober; adding or changing a route requires two synchronized edits and they can silently drift.
findings.suggestion: Move the resource-route table (pattern → API resource) into one plain .mjs module both main.ts (via a .ts wrapper or shared source) and server.mjs import, or generate server.mjs's table from the same source of truth.

findings.issue: Inline `Number(pokemon.url.match(/\/(\d+)\/?$/)?.[1])` re-implements idFromUrl from app/src/format.ts:17; an ID-parsing fix must be applied twice.

The card list's ordering is implicit (inherited from the pre-sorted speciesList in api.ts:152) rather than an explicit sort, so adding alternate orderings (e.g. by name) needs bespoke logic in home.ts while every other list sorts in speciesCards (components.ts:78).
findings.suggestion: Give cardList or speciesCards an optional ordering (or a comparator) and have home use the same path as the other lists.

findings.issue: The `types.get(x) ?? humanize(x)` label fallback is repeated in home.ts:86, move.ts:22, pokemon.ts:37 and types.ts:51; changing the fallback rule means four edits.
findings.suggestion: Expose a single labelFor(map, name) helper (or a typeLabel factory built from typeNames()) in components or format.

findings.issue: CardData carries only {id, name, extra}; a fix needing Pokémon-record data (e.g. sprites.front_default instead of the URL pattern) ripples to every caller because speciesCards/home only have references.
findings.suggestion: Accept that CardData may carry a sprite URL, or have speciesCards optionally resolve the default Pokémon record.

findings.issue: typeBadge/typeBadges use a boolean `link` flag to choose <a> vs <span>, the only flag-parameter creep in the shared layer.
findings.suggestion: Either keep the flag (it's honest) or split into linked/unlinked variants if a third mode appears.

findings.issue: .card-note exists solely for the ability page's hidden note; removing the Abilities feature leaves it dead with no signal from the code.
findings.suggestion: Co-locate or comment feature-specific CSS, or accept and sweep CSS on removals.

summary: A small, well-layered vanilla-TS app: pages are independent modules over genuinely reusable primitives (pokemonCard/speciesCards, sortableTable, section/descriptionList, pure formatters), so most fixes and the new-Items extension land in one or two obvious places. The main editability costs are the duplicated route table between the client router and server.mjs, a couple of small copy-paste warts (inline ID parsing, repeated type-label fallback), and the absence of any in-repo tests to lean on when refactoring. I'd approve this PR with the route-table duplication addressed.
